anytime_depth4.description: Anytime optimal-tree search at maximum depth 4 on hidden subsamples of CP4IM datasets (40 random de-duplicated features, 60% of rows up to 1000, min support 1; instances whose itemset lattice is under twice the budget, whose greedy tree is optimal, or whose optimum is below 10 are excluded) with a budget of 20,000 itemset-count queries (about 20% of the itemset lattice).
anytime_depth4.notes: Scaled gym experiment, not reported in the paper. Results are the gym's reference runs on the hidden test slice (deterministic: reruns are bit-identical). Solvers that fail the completeness constraint (no optimality proof on the completeness-check instances, whose budgets exceed their whole search space) or fail any run are scored with the worst value 1.0; the incomplete greedy / Top-k baselines therefore show 1.0 here (their unconstrained values are reported unranked in scores_test.json). The paper's own numbers (25 full CP4IM datasets, depths 5-7, 300 s, C++) are not on this scale and are kept under _paper_reported.

avg_primal_gap_integral.description: Primal integral (Berthold 2013) of the incumbent's primal gap |x - x*| / |x| over the evaluator-counted query budget, divided by the budget and averaged over instances; the gap is 1 before the first tree. The paper's anytime metric (Tables 2 and 3), with query effort in place of seconds.

avg_final_primal_gap.description: Primal gap of the incumbent when the budget is exhausted, averaged over instances: how close the solver ends to the optimal constrained tree.

anytime_depth5.description: Anytime optimal-tree search at maximum depth 5 on hidden subsamples of CP4IM datasets (40 random de-duplicated features, 60% of rows up to 1000, min support 1; instances whose itemset lattice is under twice the budget, whose greedy tree is optimal, or whose optimum is below 10 are excluded) with a budget of 60,000 itemset-count queries (under 8% of the itemset lattice). constraints.completeness: A solver must prove optimality on every completeness-check instance (depth 3, 10 features, budget 64x the itemset lattice). Failing it, or failing any run, scores the solver with the worst value in every metric of every experiment.

_paper_reported.note: Numbers reported in the paper (unchanged). 25 CP4IM datasets, minimum support 1, C++ implementations, wall-clock budgets; average primal integral in the paper's units. Not on the gym's scale.
